tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

content.content: use calendar versions, 2025.01 onwards, and add Cypher 25. 5.26 is the long-term-support line of the 5.x series.) **Why:** biographical memory is relational. "How's my sister?" is a hop to Maya, then to every memory `ABOUT` her. "Anyone in my family?" is a walk over typed relationships. "What did I believe before?" follows `SUPERSEDES` chains. A vector store can only find text that *looks* similar. Keeping vectors in the same database means one transaction, one consistency model, and one query that can start from a vector hit and continue along edges. Lesson 8 tabulates the needs that vectors alone don't meet. **Costs:** - A second query language (Cypher) and a less common operational skill set. - Neo4j's vector index is good but not a specialist: no BM25 + vector fusion inside the database (the `neo4j-graphrag` Python package's `HybridRetriever` combines a vector and a full-text index in the client). - On 5.26, filters run *after* the approximate search. That's why recall asks for the top 50 and filters by `user` afterwards (see D4). Neo4j 2026.01 added filtering *inside* the vector index (Cypher 25's `SEARCH` clause, with filter properties declared on the index) as a preview. That removes this cost on newer versions. - Community Edition has one user database, no fine-grained access control and no clustering. **Alternatives:** | Option | Wins when | Loses | |---|---|---| | **Vector DB only** (Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma, pgvector alone) | memory is "find similar past text"; no entities or history | multi-hop, "everything about X", contradiction handling, time | | **Postgres + pgvector** (+ recursive CTEs, or Apache AGE for openCypher) | you already run Postgres; joins are shallow; you want one familiar DB | deep or variable-length traversals get awkward and slow; graph modeling is by convention | | **Another property-graph DB** (Memgraph, FalkorDB, Amazon Neptune; embedded: LadybugDB) | Memgraph: in-memory speed and streaming; FalkorDB: Redis-based, low latency, used by Graphiti and Cognee; Neptune: managed on AWS with LPG and RDF; embedded: no server at all | most speak Cypher or openCypher, so the ideas here carry over, but GDS, APOC and vector-index details differ. Kuzu, the best-known embedded option, was archived in October 2025; LadybugDB is its maintained fork | | **Separate graph DB + vector DB** | each side at large scale, with a specialist team | two writes per memory, no shared transaction, ids to keep in sync | | **RDF triple store** (GraphDB, Stardog, Neptune RDF) + OWL | formal semantics, standard vocabularies, reasoning across organizations | heavier modeling, SPARQL, weaker vector support; overkill for one person's life | | **Document/KV store** (LangGraph `BaseStore`, Redis, Mongo) | a "user profile" document is enough | no relationships; every query is a scan or a custom index | | **Memory framework or service** (Mem0, Zep, Letta, Cognee, LangMem, Neo4j Labs `neo4j-agent-memory`) | you want memory as a product, not a project | less control over identity, time, privacy rules and evaluation; see [Other systems](#how-other-memory-systems-choose) | | **Cloud platform memory** (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory, Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank) | you already build agents on that cloud; extraction and consolidation are run for you | the provider's extraction rules and scopes; facts are a flat list searched by similarity, with no graph to traverse | | **Files the agent edits** (Anthropic's memory tool, Letta's git-backed MemFS) | the agent should curate its own notes; humans can read and diff them | no index or graph: the agent finds things with file search, and quality depends on the model's discipline | **Revisit when:** you need horizontal scale beyond one machine, hard multi-tenant isolation .... ### D11. Hybrid retrieval: vectors find where to start, the graph reasons from there **Chose:** *hybrid* in sense (b) of the [glossary](glossary.md#hybrid): vector + graph, not vector + keyword. Entities named or *meant* in the message are expanded along `ABOUT` and `RELATED` edges. **Why:** Lesson 6's rule of thumb. content.text:
Short answer: for Neo4j, the code imports only the official `neo4j` driver. Every other library the docs name is there for comparison, not as a dependency. The gaps table in [design-decisions.md:518](docs/design-decisions.md:518) lists open work, and none of it has been built yet.

## Libraries the docs mention

| Library | Used? | Why or why not |
|---|---|---|
| **`neo4j`** (official driver) | **Yes** | Every module runs plain Cypher through it. That keeps each query visible, which matters in a tutorial. |
| **GDS and APOC** | **Yes**, but as server plugins, not Python libraries | They're installed in the Docker image ([docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)). Lessons 4 and 15 call them as Cypher procedures (`CALL gds.pageRank...`). The `graphdatascience` Python client isn't used, because it would hide those calls behind Python methods. |
| **`neo4j-graphrag`** (`HybridRetriever`) | No | It comes up in D1 and D11 ([design-decisions.md:73](docs/design-decisions.md:73), [:319](docs/design-decisions.md:319)) as the ready-made way to combine full-text and vector search. Retrieval here is vector + graph, written by hand in [graphrag.py](graphrag.py) and the companion code. `import graphrag` in the code refers to that local file, not this package. |
| **`neo4j-agent-memory`** (Neo4j Labs) | No | It's in the comparison table and in the "Reasoning memory" gap. The project builds the same memory layer itself so you can read it end to end, and the docs note that Labs projects come with no support guarantees. |
| **Graphiti, Mem0, Cognee, Zep, Letta, LangMem** | No | These are memory products. D1 and "How other memory systems choose" use them to place this design. They're dropped for "less control over identity, time, privacy rules and evaluation". Graphiti is called out as the closest relative. |
| **LangGraph `BaseStore`** | No | Neo4j does that job ([glossary.md:59](docs/glossary.md:59)). LangGraph itself is used for the Lesson 7 agent, through `langchain-openai`. |
| **`neosemantics`, RDF and OWL** | No | Lesson 12 uses a lighter ontology instead, written in Python and stored in Neo4j. |

The pattern: tools that run inside the database (GDS, APOC, the vector index) are used. Python wrappers and memory frameworks that would hide the Cypher are not, because showing that Cypher is the point of the course.

## The gaps (not built)

The highest-value ones first:

- **Keyword retrieval.** This is the cheapest gap to close, and D11 calls it "a cheap, sensible next step". You'd add a Neo4j full-text index as one more retriever and merge its ranking with the vector results using reciprocal-rank fusion. `neo4j-graphrag`'s `HybridRetriever` does this out of the box. Writing it by hand would fit the course style better.
- **Memory poisoning.** This is the biggest risk. Nothing records where a memory came from, and nothing filters instruction-like text before it's stored.
- **Reflection / insights** and **reasoning memory.** Both would be new features: a scheduled LLM pass that writes higher-level `insight` memories, and stored decision traces in the style of `neo4j-agent-memory`.
- **Scale, multimodal, shared memory across users, erasure outside the graph, benchmarks (LoCoMo / LongMemEval), learned thresholds, non-English.** These are larger projects than a tutorial change.

"""Lesson 8 — the memory graph's schema. Safe to run repeatedly (IF NOT EXISTS everywhere).

    (:User:Entity {id, name, kind:'self'})
    (:Entity {id, user, name, kind, aliases, summary, embedding})   embedding: see Lesson 19
        kind: person | pet | place | organization | activity | thing
    (:User|Entity)-[:RELATED {type, said, since, until, updated_at}]->(:Entity)   life graph
        type: canonical ontology type (Lesson 12); said: the word used; until: when it ended
    (:Forgotten {user, episode, embedding})                     tombstone for /forget (Lesson 11)
    (:Memory {id, user, text, kind, importance, embedding,
              occurred_on, due_on, status,                     domain time (when it happened)
              created_at, invalidated_at, last_accessed, access_count})  system time
        kind: fact | preference | event | plan | feeling | boundary
    (:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(:Entity)                               who/what it concerns
    (:Memory)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(:Memory)                          newer version of a fact
    (:Memory)-[:FROM]->(:Episode)                               provenance
    (:Episode {id, user, started_at, ended_at, summary, mood, embedding})
    (:Episode)-[:NEXT]->(:Episode), (:Episode)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx, role, text, at})
"""
from companion.embeddings import PROFILE

STATEMENTS = [
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT entity_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Entity) REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT memory_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Memory) REQUIRE m.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT episode_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Episode) REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE INDEX memory_user_kind IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Memory) ON (m.user, m.kind)",
    "CREATE INDEX entity_user IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Entity) ON (e.user)",
    "CREATE INDEX episode_user IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Episode) ON (e.user, e.started_at)",
]


def vector_indexes(profile=PROFILE) -> list[str]:
    """One set of vector indexes per embedding model (Lesson 19): memory_vec on n.embedding for
    the default model, memory_vec_<model> on n.embedding_<model> for any other."""
    return [
        f"CREATE VECTOR INDEX {profile.index(name)} IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:{label}) ON (n.{profile.prop}) "
        f"OPTIONS {{indexConfig: {{`vector.dimensions`: {profile.dims}, "
        f"`vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}}}"
        for name, label in [("memory_vec", "Memory"), ("entity_vec", "Entity"), ("episode_vec", "Episode")]
    ]


def ensure_schema(driver) -> None:
    for stmt in STATEMENTS + vector_indexes():
        driver.execute_query(stmt)
    driver.execute_query("CALL db.awaitIndexes(120)")
        return [f"{r['id']}: {r['name']} ({r['kind']}{', ' + '/'.join(r['rel']) if r['rel'] else ''})"
                + (f" — {r['summary']}" if r["summary"] else "") for r in rows]

    def inferred_relations(self, now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        """Relatives the user never linked directly, inferred with the ontology's kinship rules
        (e.g. user -brother-> Leo -daughter-> Ana  =>  Ana is the user's niece_or_nephew).
        Entities protected by a boundary are left out."""
        edges = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (a:Entity {user: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE r.until IS NULL
              AND """ + visible("r") + """
            RETURN a.id AS src, b.id AS dst, r.type AS type
            """
        )
        found = ontology.infer_kin(edges, self.user)
        if not found:
            return []
        rows = {r["id"]: r for r in self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.id IN $ids
              AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) }
            RETURN e.id AS id, e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, e.summary AS summary
            """,
            ids=[f["id"] for f in found] + [f["via"] for f in found], now=now,
        )}
        return [{**f, **rows[f["id"]], "via_name": rows[f["via"]]["name"]}
                for f in found if f["id"] in rows and f["via"] in rows]

    @traced("store.recall", "RETRIEVER")
    def recall(self, query: str, k: int = 8, today: dt.date | None = None, touch: bool = True) -> dict:
        """What the companion knows that's relevant to `query`. `touch=False` only looks
        (the web UI's preview): it doesn't count as an access."""
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        now = clock.now_for(today)
        q = partial(self._q, now=now)  # every query below sees the conversation's clock
        vec = embed([query], query=True)[0]  # a message searched against memories (Lesson 19)
        # Core profile: every boundary + the most important stable facts and preferences.
        core = q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'boundary'}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
              RETURN m  // boundaries are never private: every persona respects them
              UNION
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
                AND m.kind IN ['fact', 'preference'] AND m.importance >= 6
                AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
              WITH m ORDER BY m.importance DESC, m.created_at DESC LIMIT 8
              RETURN m
            }
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text,
                   duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0 AS age
            ORDER BY CASE m.kind WHEN 'boundary' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, m.importance DESC
            """
        )
        for m in core:
            m["stale"] = decay.is_stale(m["kind"], m.pop("age"))
        # Semantic: vector similarity re-ranked by importance and recency (feelings fade fast).
        semantic = q(
            """
            CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes($memory_vec, 50, $vec) YIELD node AS m, score
            WHERE m.user = $user AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now) AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done'
              AND (m.kind = 'boundary' OR """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """) AND """ + visible("m") + """
            WITH collect({m: m, score: score}) AS hits
            WITH hits, reduce(top = 0.0, h IN hits | CASE WHEN h.score > top THEN h.score ELSE top END) AS top
            UNWIND hits AS h
            WITH h.m AS m, h.score AS score, top
            WHERE NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)  // sensitive: only as (near) the best match
               OR (score >= top - $margin AND score >= $floor)
            // Age since it was stored or last *confirmed* by the user, on the conversation's clock.
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.occurred_on AS occurred_on,
                   m.importance AS importance, coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AS sensitive,
                   round(score, 3) AS score, duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0 AS age
            """,
            vec=vec, margin=SENSITIVE_MARGIN, floor=SENSITIVE_FLOOR,
        )
        # Decay (Lesson 13) in Python, where the curve is unit-tested: drop dormant memories,
        # then order by match + strength.
        dormant = [{"id": m["id"], "kind": m["kind"], "text": m["text"], "score": m["score"],
                    "strength": round(decay.strength(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"]), 3)}
                   for m in semantic if decay.is_dormant(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"])]
        semantic = [m for m in semantic if not decay.is_dormant(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"])]
        # Relevance (Lesson 18): mark what the vector search returned only because it had to
        # return something. Weak matches go after strong ones and are labelled in the prompt.
        # A current status ("at the gym" until 14:00) is never weak: it's context for any
        # message, like "Recently" below ("what am I doing?" scored -8.9 against it).
        # Lesson 19: a model whose scores DO separate (Qwen3-8B) decides with its own score,
        # and the cross-encoder isn't needed (it called "how is my kid doing?" vs "Mark's son
        # Logan attends Elk Grove Elementary" weak).
        if PROFILE.weak_below is not None:
            scores, cut = [m["score"] for m in semantic], PROFILE.weak_below
        else:
            scores, cut = relevance(query, [m["text"] for m in semantic]), RELEVANCE_MIN
        for m, r in zip(semantic, scores):
            m["relevance"] = round(r, 3 if PROFILE.weak_below is not None else 2)
            m["weak"] = r < cut and m["kind"] != "status"
        semantic = sorted(
            ({**m, "rank": round(decay.rank(m["score"], m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"]), 3),
              "stale": decay.is_stale(m["kind"], m["age"])} for m in semantic),
            key=lambda m: (m["weak"], -m["rank"]))[:k]
        # History ("where did I live before?"): embeddings can't express "before", so walk the
        # graph instead — older versions of the best-matching current memories.
        strong = [m for m in semantic if not m["weak"]]  # no history for a match that isn't about this
        top = max((m["score"] for m in strong), default=0)
        best = [m["id"] for m in sorted(strong, key=lambda m: -m["score"])[:3] if m["score"] >= top - 0.02]
        history = q(
            """
            MATCH (cur:Memory)-[:SUPERSEDES*1..3]->(m:Memory) WHERE cur.id IN $ids AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """
              AND """ + visible("m") + """
            WITH cur, m AS old
            RETURN old.id AS id, old.text AS text, date(old.invalidated_at) AS until, cur.text AS replaced_by
            """,
            ids=best,
        )
        # "Anyone in my family / at work...": the ontology says which relation types each group
        # covers, and inference adds relatives nobody linked directly (a brother's daughter).
        groups = ontology.groups_in(query)
        group_types = sorted(set().union(*(ontology.types_in_group(g) for g in groups))) if groups else []
        inferred = self.inferred_relations(now)
        inferred_ids = [i["id"] for i in inferred if i["relation"] in group_types]
        # Graph hop: entities named (or meant) in the message -> their memories and relations.
        entities = q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self'
                AND any(n IN [e.name] + coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE size(n) > 2 AND toLower($q) CONTAINS toLower(n))
              RETURN e
              UNION
              CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes($entity_vec, 50, $vec) YIELD node AS e, score
              WITH e, score WHERE e.user = $user AND e.kind <> 'self' AND score >= $hop
              RETURN e ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 3
              UNION  // "anyone in my family / at work...": everyone in that group of relations
              MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e:Entity) WHERE r.type IN $types AND r.until IS NULL
              RETURN e
              UNION  // ...including inferred relatives
              MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.id IN $inferred
              RETURN e
            }
            WITH e WHERE NOT EXISTS {  // entities protected by a boundary are never surfaced
              MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) }
              AND """ + entity_visible("e") + """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e) WHERE r.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("r") + """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(e)
              WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now) AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done' AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)
                AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            WITH e, r, m ORDER BY m.importance DESC
            WITH e, head(collect(r.type)) AS relation,
                 collect(DISTINCT m {.id, .kind, .text, .importance,
                                     age: duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0})[..20] AS memories
            // Its links to other entities, both directions and up to two steps (Logan -likes->
            // Minecraft is found from either end; "my son's friend Max" -> Max's dog), each end
            // labelled with its relation to the user if it has one. Never through the user, a
            // protected entity or a link this persona can't see.
            WITH e, relation, memories, COLLECT {
              MATCH p = (e)-[:RELATED*1..2]-(o:Entity)
              WHERE all(x IN nodes(p)[1..] WHERE NOT x:User AND """ + entity_visible("x") + """
                        AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b2:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(x)
                                         WHERE b2.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b2.valid_until IS NULL OR b2.valid_until > $now) })
                AND all(r2 IN relationships(p) WHERE r2.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("r2") + """)
              UNWIND relationships(p) AS r2
              WITH DISTINCT r2, startNode(r2) AS s, endNode(r2) AS t
              RETURN {source: s.name, type: r2.type, target: t.name,
                      source_rel: COLLECT { MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[u:RELATED]->(s) WHERE u.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("u") + """ RETURN u.type }[0],
                      target_rel: COLLECT { MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[u:RELATED]->(t) WHERE u.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("u") + """ RETURN u.type }[0]}
              LIMIT 15
            } AS links
            RETURN e.id AS id, e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, e.summary AS summary, relation, memories, links
            LIMIT 12
            """,
            q=query, vec=vec, hop=ENTITY_HOP_SCORE, types=group_types, inferred=inferred_ids,
        )
        for e in entities:  # same decay rule as semantic recall
            e["memories"] = [m for m in e["memories"]
                             if not decay.is_dormant(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"])][:5]
        by_id = {i["id"]: i for i in inferred}
        for e in entities:
            if not e["relation"] and e["id"] in by_id:
                e["relation"] = f"{by_id[e['id']]['relation']}, inferred via {by_id[e['id']]['via_name']}"
        people = q(
            """
            MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e:Entity) WHERE r.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("r") + """
              AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) }
            RETURN e.id AS id, e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, r.type AS relation, e.summary AS summary
            ORDER BY e.kind, e.name LIMIT 25
            """
        )
        people += [{"id": i["id"], "name": i["name"], "kind": i["kind"], "summary": i["summary"],
                    "relation": f"{i['relation']}, inferred via {i['via_name']}"} for i in inferred]
        followups = q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
            WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now) AND m.due_on IS NOT NULL
              AND m.due_on >= $today - duration({days: 14}) AND m.due_on <= $today + duration({days: 14})
              AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m.due_on AS due_on,
                   coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AS sensitive ORDER BY m.due_on
            """,
            today=today,
        )
        # Yearly dates (birthdays, anniversaries) coming up in the next two weeks.
        upcoming = []
        for m in q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.annual_date IS NOT NULL AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
              AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m.annual_date AS annual_date,
                   coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AS sensitive
            """
        ):
            when = _next_occurrence(m["annual_date"], today)
            if when and when <= today + dt.timedelta(days=14):
                upcoming.append({**m, "on": when})
        upcoming.sort(key=lambda m: m["on"])
        # Situational memories that ended in the last day ("at the gym" until 14:00): no longer
        # true, but a friend would ask how it went.
        recent = q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
              AND m.valid_until <= $now AND m.valid_until > $now - duration({hours: $hours})
              AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.valid_until AS until,
                   coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AS sensitive ORDER BY m.valid_until DESC LIMIT 5
            """,
            hours=RECENT_HOURS,
        )
        episodes = q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE ep.summary IS NOT NULL
              AND (ep.agent IS NULL OR ep.agent = $agent)  // summaries can quote private things
            RETURN ep.started_at AS at, ep.summary AS summary, ep.mood AS mood
            ORDER BY ep.started_at DESC LIMIT 3
            """
        )
        touched = [m["id"] for m in semantic if not m["weak"]] + [m["id"] for e in entities for m in e["memories"]]
        if touch:
            q(
            """
                MATCH (m:Memory) WHERE m.id IN $ids
                SET m.last_accessed = datetime(), m.access_count = coalesce(m.access_count, 0) + 1
                """,
                ids=touched,
            )
        return {"dormant": dormant, "relevance_min": RELEVANCE_MIN if PROFILE.weak_below is None else PROFILE.weak_below,
                "relevance_by": "cross-encoder" if PROFILE.weak_below is None else "vector score", "core": core, "semantic": semantic, "entities": entities, "people": people,
                "followups": followups, "upcoming": upcoming, "history": history, "episodes": episodes,
                "recent": recent}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ consolidation
    def consolidate(self, today: dt.date | None = None, writer=None, prune: bool = True) -> list[str]:
        """Background upkeep (Lesson 13). Run after a conversation, or nightly:

        1. lapse   open plans long past due stop being followed up
        2. roll up repeated situational memories ("at the gym" x3) into one lasting pattern,
                   written by `writer(user, texts, today) -> MemoryOut | None` (an LLM call,
                   injected so tests can use a fake); the members are marked consolidated
        3. prune   delete dormant, low-importance statuses and feelings (data minimization),
                   but only once they're rolled up or older than the pattern window: pruning
                   earlier would delete the repeats before they could ever form a pattern
        4. orphans entities with no memory and no link left are deleted (see _drop_orphans)

        Everything else is kept: events stay as history even when dormant."""
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        now = clock.now_for(today)
        q = partial(self._q, now=now)
        log = [f"plan lapsed: {r['text']}" for r in q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
            WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.due_on < date($now) - duration({days: $days})
            SET m.status = 'lapsed' RETURN m.text AS text
            """, days=LAPSE_AFTER_DAYS)]

        if writer is not None:
            rows = q(
                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.consolidated_at IS NULL
                  AND m.kind IN ['event', 'status', 'feeling'] AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)
                  AND NOT coalesce(m.private, false)  // a shared pattern must not be built from private memories
                  AND m.created_at > $now - duration({days: $days})
                  AND m[$vprop] IS NOT NULL  // not yet re-embedded for this model (Lesson 19)
                RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m[$vprop] AS vec ORDER BY m.created_at
                """, days=PATTERN_WINDOW_DAYS)
            if PROFILE.cluster_instruction:  # this model groups better with an instruction (Lesson 19)
                for r, v in zip(rows, embed_for_clustering([r["text"] for r in rows])):
                    r["vec"] = v
            for group in _clusters(rows, PATTERN_SIMILARITY, PATTERN_MIN):
                pattern = writer(self.user_name, [r["text"] for r in group], today)
                if pattern is None:
                    continue
                log += self._write(lambda: self._store_pattern(pattern, group, today, now))
        if prune:
            log += self._prune(now)
        log += self._drop_orphans()
        return log

    def _drop_orphans(self) -> list[str]:
        """4. orphans  an entity nothing points at any more — no memory (current or retired)
        is about it and it has no link, past or present — is left over from a forget, a prune
        or an extraction that named it without saying how it connects ("Disney+"). It would
        float alone in the life graph and be matched by recall for nothing, so it goes."""
        gone = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE NOT e:User
              AND NOT EXISTS { (e)<-[:ABOUT]-(:Memory) } AND NOT EXISTS { (e)-[:RELATED]-() }
            WITH e, e.name AS name DETACH DELETE e RETURN name
            """
        )
        return [f"dropped {len(gone)} unconnected entities: {', '.join(sorted(g['name'] for g in gone))}"] if gone else []

def vector_indexes(profile=PROFILE) -> list[str]:
    """One set of vector indexes per embedding model (Lesson 19): memory_vec on n.embedding for
    the default model, memory_vec_<model> on n.embedding_<model> for any other."""
    return [
        f"CREATE VECTOR INDEX {profile.index(name)} IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:{label}) ON (n.{profile.prop}) "
        f"OPTIONS {{indexConfig: {{`vector.dimensions`: {profile.dims}, "
        f"`vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}}}"
        for name, label in [("memory_vec", "Memory"), ("entity_vec", "Entity"), ("episode_vec", "Episode")]
    ]


def ensure_schema(driver) -> None:
    for stmt in STATEMENTS + vector_indexes():
        driver.execute_query(stmt)
    driver.execute_query("CALL db.awaitIndexes(120)")

                + (f" — {r['summary']}" if r["summary"] else "") for r in rows]

    def inferred_relations(self, now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        """Relatives the user never linked directly, inferred with the ontology's kinship rules
        (e.g. user -brother-> Leo -daughter-> Ana  =>  Ana is the user's niece_or_nephew).
        Entities protected by a boundary are left out."""
        edges = self._q(
            """
            MATCH (a:Entity {user: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(b:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE r.until IS NULL
              AND """ + visible("r") + """
            RETURN a.id AS src, b.id AS dst, r.type AS type
            """
        )
        found = ontology.infer_kin(edges, self.user)
        if not found:
            return []
        rows = {r["id"]: r for r in self._q(
            """
            MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.id IN $ids
              AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) }
            RETURN e.id AS id, e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, e.summary AS summary
            """,
            ids=[f["id"] for f in found] + [f["via"] for f in found], now=now,
        )}
        return [{**f, **rows[f["id"]], "via_name": rows[f["via"]]["name"]}
                for f in found if f["id"] in rows and f["via"] in rows]

    @traced("store.recall", "RETRIEVER")
    def recall(self, query: str, k: int = 8, today: dt.date | None = None, touch: bool = True) -> dict:
        """What the companion knows that's relevant to `query`. `touch=False` only looks
        (the web UI's preview): it doesn't count as an access."""
        today = today or dt.date.today()
        now = clock.now_for(today)
        q = partial(self._q, now=now)  # every query below sees the conversation's clock
        vec = embed([query], query=True)[0]  # a message searched against memories (Lesson 19)
        # Core profile: every boundary + the most important stable facts and preferences.
        core = q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'boundary'}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
              RETURN m  // boundaries are never private: every persona respects them
              UNION
              MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
                AND m.kind IN ['fact', 'preference'] AND m.importance >= 6
                AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
              WITH m ORDER BY m.importance DESC, m.created_at DESC LIMIT 8
              RETURN m
            }
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text,
                   duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0 AS age
            ORDER BY CASE m.kind WHEN 'boundary' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, m.importance DESC
            """
        )
        for m in core:
            m["stale"] = decay.is_stale(m["kind"], m.pop("age"))
        # Semantic: vector similarity re-ranked by importance and recency (feelings fade fast).
        semantic = q(
            """
            CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes($memory_vec, 50, $vec) YIELD node AS m, score
            WHERE m.user = $user AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now) AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done'
              AND (m.kind = 'boundary' OR """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """) AND """ + visible("m") + """
            WITH collect({m: m, score: score}) AS hits
            WITH hits, reduce(top = 0.0, h IN hits | CASE WHEN h.score > top THEN h.score ELSE top END) AS top
            UNWIND hits AS h
            WITH h.m AS m, h.score AS score, top
            WHERE NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)  // sensitive: only as (near) the best match
               OR (score >= top - $margin AND score >= $floor)
            // Age since it was stored or last *confirmed* by the user, on the conversation's clock.
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.occurred_on AS occurred_on,
                   m.importance AS importance, coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AS sensitive,
                   round(score, 3) AS score, duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0 AS age
            """,
            vec=vec, margin=SENSITIVE_MARGIN, floor=SENSITIVE_FLOOR,
        )
        # Decay (Lesson 13) in Python, where the curve is unit-tested: drop dormant memories,
        # then order by match + strength.
        dormant = [{"id": m["id"], "kind": m["kind"], "text": m["text"], "score": m["score"],
                    "strength": round(decay.strength(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"]), 3)}
                   for m in semantic if decay.is_dormant(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"])]
        semantic = [m for m in semantic if not decay.is_dormant(m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"])]
        # Relevance (Lesson 18): mark what the vector search returned only because it had to
        # return something. Weak matches go after strong ones and are labelled in the prompt.
        # A current status ("at the gym" until 14:00) is never weak: it's context for any
        # message, like "Recently" below ("what am I doing?" scored -8.9 against it).
        # Lesson 19: a model whose scores DO separate (Qwen3-8B) decides with its own score,
        # and the cross-encoder isn't needed (it called "how is my kid doing?" vs "Mark's son
        # Logan attends Elk Grove Elementary" weak).
        if PROFILE.weak_below is not None:
            scores, cut = [m["score"] for m in semantic], PROFILE.weak_below
        else:
            scores, cut = relevance(query, [m["text"] for m in semantic]), RELEVANCE_MIN
        for m, r in zip(semantic, scores):
            m["relevance"] = round(r, 3 if PROFILE.weak_below is not None else 2)
            m["weak"] = r < cut and m["kind"] != "status"
        semantic = sorted(
            ({**m, "rank": round(decay.rank(m["score"], m["importance"], m["kind"], m["age"]), 3),
              "stale": decay.is_stale(m["kind"], m["age"])} for m in semantic),
            key=lambda m: (m["weak"], -m["rank"]))[:k]
        # History ("where did I live before?"): embeddings can't express "before", so walk the
        # graph instead — older versions of the best-matching current memories.
        strong = [m for m in semantic if not m["weak"]]  # no history for a match that isn't about this
        top = max((m["score"] for m in strong), default=0)
        best = [m["id"] for m in sorted(strong, key=lambda m: -m["score"])[:3] if m["score"] >= top - 0.02]
        history = q(
            """
            MATCH (cur:Memory)-[:SUPERSEDES*1..3]->(m:Memory) WHERE cur.id IN $ids AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """
              AND """ + visible("m") + """
            WITH cur, m AS old
            RETURN old.id AS id, old.text AS text, date(old.invalidated_at) AS until, cur.text AS replaced_by
            """,
            ids=best,
        )
        # "Anyone in my family / at work...": the ontology says which relation types each group
        # covers, and inference adds relatives nobody linked directly (a brother's daughter).
        groups = ontology.groups_in(query)
        group_types = sorted(set().union(*(ontology.types_in_group(g) for g in groups))) if groups else []
        inferred = self.inferred_relations(now)
        inferred_ids = [i["id"] for i in inferred if i["relation"] in group_types]
        # Graph hop: entities named (or meant) in the message -> their memories and relations.
        entities = q(
            """
            CALL () {
              MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.kind <> 'self'
                AND any(n IN [e.name] + coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE size(n) > 2 AND toLower($q) CONTAINS toLower(n))
              RETURN e
              UNION
              CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes($entity_vec, 50, $vec) YIELD node AS e, score
              WITH e, score WHERE e.user = $user AND e.kind <> 'self' AND score >= $hop
              RETURN e ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 3
              UNION  // "anyone in my family / at work...": everyone in that group of relations
              MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e:Entity) WHERE r.type IN $types AND r.until IS NULL
              RETURN e
              UNION  // ...including inferred relatives
              MATCH (e:Entity {user: $user}) WHERE e.id IN $inferred
              RETURN e
            }
            WITH e WHERE NOT EXISTS {  // entities protected by a boundary are never surfaced
              MATCH (b:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(e) WHERE b.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b.valid_until IS NULL OR b.valid_until > $now) }
              AND """ + entity_visible("e") + """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e) WHERE r.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("r") + """
            OPTIONAL MATCH (m:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(e)
              WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now) AND coalesce(m.status, '') <> 'done' AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)
                AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            WITH e, r, m ORDER BY m.importance DESC
            WITH e, head(collect(r.type)) AS relation,
                 collect(DISTINCT m {.id, .kind, .text, .importance,
                                     age: duration.inSeconds(coalesce(m.last_confirmed, m.created_at), $now).seconds / 86400.0})[..20] AS memories
            // Its links to other entities, both directions and up to two steps (Logan -likes->
            // Minecraft is found from either end; "my son's friend Max" -> Max's dog), each end
            // labelled with its relation to the user if it has one. Never through the user, a
            // protected entity or a link this persona can't see.
            WITH e, relation, memories, COLLECT {

              WHERE all(x IN nodes(p)[1..] WHERE NOT x:User AND """ + entity_visible("x") + """
                        AND NOT EXISTS { MATCH (b2:Memory {kind: 'boundary'})-[:ABOUT]->(x)
                                         WHERE b2.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (b2.valid_until IS NULL OR b2.valid_until > $now) })
                AND all(r2 IN relationships(p) WHERE r2.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("r2") + """)
              UNWIND relationships(p) AS r2
              WITH DISTINCT r2, startNode(r2) AS s, endNode(r2) AS t
              RETURN {source: s.name, type: r2.type, target: t.name,
                      source_rel: COLLECT { MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[u:RELATED]->(s) WHERE u.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("u") + """ RETURN u.type }[0],
                      target_rel: COLLECT { MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[u:RELATED]->(t) WHERE u.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("u") + """ RETURN u.type }[0]}

            RETURN e.id AS id, e.name AS name, e.kind AS kind, e.summary AS summary, relation, memories, links

            MATCH (:User {id: $user})-[r:RELATED]->(e:Entity) WHERE r.until IS NULL AND """ + visible("r") + """

            ORDER BY e.kind, e.name LIMIT 25

            """,

        upcoming = []

            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.annual_date IS NOT NULL AND m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND (m.valid_until IS NULL OR m.valid_until > $now)
              AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m.annual_date AS annual_date,

        upcoming.sort(key=lambda m: m["on"])

        # true, but a friend would ask how it went.
        recent = q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL
              AND m.valid_until <= $now AND m.valid_until > $now - duration({hours: $hours})
              AND """ + NOT_PROTECTED + """ AND """ + visible("m") + """
            RETURN m.id AS id, m.kind AS kind, m.text AS text, m.valid_until AS until,
                   coalesce(m.sensitive, false) AS sensitive ORDER BY m.valid_until DESC LIMIT 5
            """,
            hours=RECENT_HOURS,
        )
        episodes = q(
            """
            MATCH (ep:Episode {user: $user}) WHERE ep.summary IS NOT NULL
              AND (ep.agent IS NULL OR ep.agent = $agent)  // summaries can quote private things
            RETURN ep.started_at AS at, ep.summary AS summary, ep.mood AS mood
            ORDER BY ep.started_at DESC LIMIT 3

    def consolidate(self, today: dt.date | None = None, writer=None, prune: bool = True) -> list[str]:
        """Background upkeep (Lesson 13). Run after a conversation, or nightly:

        1. lapse   open plans long past due stop being followed up
        2. roll up repeated situational memories ("at the gym" x3) into one lasting pattern,
                   written by `writer(user, texts, today) -> MemoryOut | None` (an LLM call,
                   injected so tests can use a fake); the members are marked consolidated
        3. prune   delete dormant, low-importance statuses and feelings (data minimization),
                   but only once they're rolled up or older than the pattern window: pruning
                   earlier would delete the repeats before they could ever form a pattern
        4. orphans entities with no memory and no link left are deleted (see _drop_orphans)

        Everything else is kept: events stay as history even when dormant."""

        now = clock.now_for(today)
        q = partial(self._q, now=now)
        log = [f"plan lapsed: {r['text']}" for r in q(
            """
            MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user, kind: 'plan', status: 'open'})
            WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.due_on < date($now) - duration({days: $days})
            SET m.status = 'lapsed' RETURN m.text AS text
            """, days=LAPSE_AFTER_DAYS)]

        if writer is not None:
            rows = q(
                """
                MATCH (m:Memory {user: $user}) WHERE m.invalidated_at IS NULL AND m.consolidated_at IS NULL
                  AND m.kind IN ['event', 'status', 'feeling'] AND NOT coalesce(m.sensitive, false)
                  AND NOT coalesce(m.private, false)  // a shared pattern must not be built from private memories
                  AND m.created_at > $now - duration({days: $days})
                  AND m[$vprop] IS NOT NULL  // not yet re-embedded for this model (Lesson 19)
                RETURN m.id AS id, m.text AS text, m[$vprop] AS vec ORDER BY m.created_at
                """, days=PATTERN_WINDOW_DAYS)

                for r, v in zip(rows, embed_for_clustering([r["text"] for r in rows])):
                    r["vec"] = v
            for group in _clusters(rows, PATTERN_SIMILARITY, PATTERN_MIN):
                pattern = writer(self.user_name, [r["text"] for r in group], today)
                if pattern is None:
                    continue
                log += self._write(lambda: self._store_pattern(pattern, group, today, now))
        if prune:
            log += self._prune(now)
        log += self._drop_orphans()
        return log

    def _drop_orphans(self) -> list[str]:
        """4. orphans  an entity nothing points at any more — no memory (current or retired)

"""Lesson 13 — decay: how relevant a memory still is, as it ages.

Validity (clock.py, `valid_until`) answers "is it still TRUE?". Decay answers "is it still
WORTH BRINGING UP?". They are different: "Riley felt tired" was true on 2026-11-18 forever,
but a month later nobody should mention it.

strength = importance/10 x 0.5 ** (age / half-life of its kind)

- age counts from when it was stored or last CONFIRMED by the user (saying it again resets
  the clock, like spaced repetition). Being recalled does not count: otherwise anything
  recalled once would keep itself alive.
- facts, preferences, boundaries and plans don't decay. A fact doesn't get less true with age;
  it may get STALE, and the companion should check it rather than drop it (see `is_stale`).
- below DORMANT_BELOW a memory is dormant: kept in the graph, left out of recall.
  Milestones (importance >= MILESTONE) never go dormant.

Pure functions, so the curve has unit tests (tests/test_13_time.py).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

HALF_LIFE_DAYS: dict[str, float | None] = {
    "status": 1,       # "at the gym": already expired via valid_until; decays in a day after
    "feeling": 7,      # "tired", "excited about the trip"
    "event": 90,       # "went to a concert"
    "fact": None, "preference": None, "boundary": None, "plan": None,
}
DORMANT_BELOW = 0.05
MILESTONE = 8          # importance at which an event is a life milestone: never dormant
STALE_DAYS = 365       # a fact not confirmed for this long is worth checking
WEIGHT_MATCH, WEIGHT_STRENGTH = 0.6, 0.4


def strength(importance: int, kind: str, age_days: float) -> float:
    half_life = HALF_LIFE_DAYS.get(kind)
    base = importance / 10
    if not half_life or age_days <= 0:
        return base
    return base * 0.5 ** (age_days / half_life)


def is_dormant(importance: int, kind: str, age_days: float) -> bool:
    return importance < MILESTONE and strength(importance, kind, age_days) < DORMANT_BELOW


def rank(score: float, importance: int, kind: str, age_days: float) -> float:
    """Recall order: how well it matches the message, plus how strong it still is."""
    return WEIGHT_MATCH * score + WEIGHT_STRENGTH * strength(importance, kind, age_days)


def is_stale(kind: str, age_days: float) -> bool:
    return kind == "fact" and age_days > STALE_DAYS


def days_until_dormant(importance: int, kind: str) -> float | None:
    """For the lesson's table: how long until a memory stops being recalled."""
    half_life = HALF_LIFE_DAYS.get(kind)
    if not half_life or importance >= MILESTONE:
        return None
    import math
    ratio = DORMANT_BELOW / (importance / 10)
    return 0.0 if ratio >= 1 else half_life * math.log(ratio, 0.5)

strength = importance/10 x 0.5 ** (age / half-life of its kind)

- age counts from when it was stored or last CONFIRMED by the user (saying it again resets
  the clock, like spaced repetition). Being recalled does not count: otherwise anything
  recalled once would keep itself alive.
- facts, preferences, boundaries and plans don't decay. A fact doesn't get less true with age;
  it may get STALE, and the companion should check it rather than drop it (see `is_stale`).
- below DORMANT_BELOW a memory is dormant: kept in the graph, left out of recall.
  Milestones (importance >= MILESTONE) never go dormant.

Pure functions, so the curve has unit tests (tests/test_13_time.py).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

HALF_LIFE_DAYS: dict[str, float | None] = {
    "status": 1,       # "at the gym": already expired via valid_until; decays in a day after
    "feeling": 7,      # "tired", "excited about the trip"
    "event": 90,       # "went to a concert"
    "fact": None, "preference": None, "boundary": None, "plan": None,
}
DORMANT_BELOW = 0.05
MILESTONE = 8          # importance at which an event is a life milestone: never dormant
STALE_DAYS = 365       # a fact not confirmed for this long is worth checking
WEIGHT_MATCH, WEIGHT_STRENGTH = 0.6, 0.4


def strength(importance: int, kind: str, age_days: float) -> float:
    half_life = HALF_LIFE_DAYS.get(kind)
    base = importance / 10
    if not half_life or age_days <= 0:
        return base
    return base * 0.5 ** (age_days / half_life)


def is_dormant(importance: int, kind: str, age_days: float) -> bool:
    return importance < MILESTONE and strength(importance, kind, age_days) < DORMANT_BELOW


def rank(score: float, importance: int, kind: str, age_days: float) -> float:
    """Recall order: how well it matches the message, plus how strong it still is."""
    return WEIGHT_MATCH * score + WEIGHT_STRENGTH * strength(importance, kind, age_days)


def is_stale(kind: str, age_days: float) -> bool:
    return kind == "fact" and age_days > STALE_DAYS


def days_until_dormant(importance: int, kind: str) -> float | None:
    """For the lesson's table: how long until a memory stops being recalled."""
    half_life = HALF_LIFE_DAYS.get(kind)
    if not half_life or importance >= MILESTONE:
        return None
    import math
    ratio = DORMANT_BELOW / (importance / 10)
    return 0.0 if ratio >= 1 else half_life * math.log(ratio, 0.5)

"""Lesson 8 — the memory graph's schema. Safe to run repeatedly (IF NOT EXISTS everywhere).

    (:User:Entity {id, name, kind:'self'})
    (:Entity {id, user, name, kind, aliases, summary, embedding})   embedding: see Lesson 19
        kind: person | pet | place | organization | activity | thing
    (:User|Entity)-[:RELATED {type, said, since, until, updated_at}]->(:Entity)   life graph
        type: canonical ontology type (Lesson 12); said: the word used; until: when it ended
    (:Forgotten {user, episode, embedding})                     tombstone for /forget (Lesson 11)
    (:Memory {id, user, text, kind, importance, embedding,
              occurred_on, due_on, status,                     domain time (when it happened)
              created_at, invalidated_at, last_accessed, access_count})  system time
        kind: fact | preference | event | plan | feeling | boundary
    (:Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(:Entity)                               who/what it concerns
    (:Memory)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(:Memory)                          newer version of a fact
    (:Memory)-[:FROM]->(:Episode)                               provenance
    (:Episode {id, user, started_at, ended_at, summary, mood, embedding})
    (:Episode)-[:NEXT]->(:Episode), (:Episode)-[:HAS_TURN]->(:Turn {idx, role, text, at})
"""
from companion.embeddings import PROFILE

STATEMENTS = [
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT entity_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Entity) REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT memory_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Memory) REQUIRE m.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE CONSTRAINT episode_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Episode) REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE",
    "CREATE INDEX memory_user_kind IF NOT EXISTS FOR (m:Memory) ON (m.user, m.kind)",
    "CREATE INDEX entity_user IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Entity) ON (e.user)",
    "CREATE INDEX episode_user IF NOT EXISTS FOR (e:Episode) ON (e.user, e.started_at)",
]


def vector_indexes(profile=PROFILE) -> list[str]:
    """One set of vector indexes per embedding model (Lesson 19): memory_vec on n.embedding for
    the default model, memory_vec_<model> on n.embedding_<model> for any other."""
    return [
        f"CREATE VECTOR INDEX {profile.index(name)} IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:{label}) ON (n.{profile.prop}) "
        f"OPTIONS {{indexConfig: {{`vector.dimensions`: {profile.dims}, "
        f"`vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}}}"
        for name, label in [("memory_vec", "Memory"), ("entity_vec", "Entity"), ("episode_vec", "Episode")]
    ]


def ensure_schema(driver) -> None:
    for stmt in STATEMENTS + vector_indexes():
        driver.execute_query(stmt)
    driver.execute_query("CALL db.awaitIndexes(120)")

# An entity this close to the message (index score) is looked up by the graph hop.

# Keyword search (D11). Embeddings blur rare exact words (a medication name, a product code),
# so a full-text (BM25) search runs beside the vector search. Its hits join the candidates,
# and the two rankings are fused with reciprocal-rank fusion: each list votes 1 / (RRF_K +
# position). Only ranks are combined, never BM25 and cosine scores, which aren't comparable.
# 60 is the constant from the RRF paper (Cormack et al., 2009) and the usual default.
KEYWORD_LIMIT = 20
RRF_K = 60


def keyword_query(text: str, user: str) -> str | None:
    """A Lucene query for the message's words, limited to this user's memories. Lowercasing
    every word means AND / OR / NOT can't act as operators, and \\w+ drops the characters
    Lucene treats as syntax. None when the message has no words ("?!")."""
    words = " ".join(w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\w+", text))
    if not words:
        return None
    return f'text:({words}) AND user:"{user.replace(chr(92), "").replace(chr(34), "")}"'


def rrf(*rankings: list[str], k: int = RRF_K) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Reciprocal-rank fusion: an id's score is the sum of 1 / (k + position) over the lists
    it appears in (positions start at 1). Being near the top of both lists beats being first
    in only one of them."""
    fused: dict[str, float] = {}
    for ranking in rankings:
        for pos, item in enumerate(ranking, start=1):
            fused[item] = fused.get(item, 0.0) + 1 / (k + pos)
    return fused

"""Lesson 8 — the memory schema. Schema setup must be idempotent: running it twice is a test."""
from companion.schema import ensure_schema
from conftest import rows


def test_schema_is_idempotent_and_complete(driver):
    ensure_schema(driver)
    ensure_schema(driver)  # IF NOT EXISTS everywhere: the second run must not fail
    constraints = {r["name"] for r in rows(driver, "SHOW CONSTRAINTS YIELD name RETURN name")}
    assert {"entity_id", "memory_id", "episode_id"} <= constraints
    indexes = {r["name"]: r["state"] for r in rows(driver, "SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, state RETURN name, state")}
    for name in ["memory_vec", "entity_vec", "episode_vec", "memory_user_kind"]:
        assert indexes.get(name) == "ONLINE", name


def test_memory_ids_are_unique(store):
    from neo4j.exceptions import ConstraintError
    import pytest

    store._q("CREATE (:Memory {id: 'm_dup', user: $user})")
    ), today=T)

        block = format_context(store.recall(question, today=T, touch=False), T)
        assert "Logan (your son) likes Minecraft" in block, block


def test_a_protected_entity_is_not_reached_through_a_link(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(
        entities=[EntityOut(name="Logan", kind="person"), EntityOut(name="Dana", kind="person")],
        relations=[RelationOut(source="user", target="Logan", type="son"),
                   RelationOut(source="Logan", target="Dana", type="mother")],
        memories=[m("Pytest doesn't want to talk about Dana", "boundary", about=["Dana"], importance=9)],
    ), today=T)
    r = store.recall("how is Logan?", today=T, touch=False)
    links = [l for e in r["entities"] for l in e["links"]]
    assert "Logan" in [e["name"] for e in r["entities"]]
    assert all("Dana" not in (l["source"], l["target"]) for l in links), links


def test_entity_hop_reaches_two_steps_out(store):
    store.apply(Extraction(
        entities=[EntityOut(name="Logan", kind="person"), EntityOut(name="Max", kind="person"),
                  EntityOut(name="Biscuit", kind="pet")],
        relations=[RelationOut(source="user", target="Logan", type="son"),
                   RelationOut(source="Logan", target="Max", type="friend"),
                   RelationOut(source="Max", target="Biscuit", type="pet")],
        memories=[m("Pytest's son Logan is 7 years old", about=["Logan"])],
    ), today=T)
    block = format_context(store.recall("how is Logan doing?", today=T, touch=False), T)
    assert "Max is Logan (your son)'s friend" in block and "Biscuit is Max's pet" in block, block

@pytest.mark.parametrize("text,expected", [
    ("Is the XK-4471 safe?", 'text:(is the xk 4471 safe) AND user:"user:pytest"'),
    ("cats AND dogs OR NOT birds", 'text:(cats and dogs or not birds) AND user:"user:pytest"'),  # no operators
    ('quote " and (paren) *star*', 'text:(quote and paren star) AND user:"user:pytest"'),        # no syntax
    ("?!", None),
])
def test_keyword_query_is_plain_words_for_this_user(text, expected):
    assert keyword_query(text, "user:pytest") == expected


def test_rrf_rewards_agreement_between_rankings():
    fused = rrf(["a", "b", "c"], ["b", "c"])
    assert fused["b"] > fused["a"]                          # 2nd + 1st beats 1st alone
    assert fused["a"] == pytest.approx(1 / 61)
    assert sorted(fused, key=fused.get, reverse=True) == ["b", "c", "a"]


def test_a_rare_word_is_found_when_the_vector_search_misses_it(store):
    """The vector index on 5.26 filters by user *after* its top 50 (D4). Fill that top 50
    with another user's memories that sit right on the message, and only the full-text
    index, which filters by user inside Lucene, still finds this user's memory."""
    store.apply(Extraction(memories=[m("Pytest bought a Zentrix XK4471 router at a garage sale")]), today=T)
    question = "my XK4471 keeps dropping the wifi"
    other = "user:pytest-crowd"
    store._q(
        """
        UNWIND range(1, 55) AS i
        CREATE (n:Memory {id: 'crowd_' + i, user: $other, kind: 'fact', importance: 5,
                          text: 'Someone else\\'s router drops the wifi, note ' + i, created_at: datetime()})
        WITH n CALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(n, $vprop, $vec)
        """,
        other=other, vec=embed([question], query=True)[0],
    )
    try:
        r = store.recall(question, today=T, touch=False)
        hit = next((x for x in r["semantic"] if "XK4471" in x["text"]), None)
        assert hit is not None, [x["text"] for x in r["semantic"]]
        assert hit["keyword_rank"] == 1 and hit["bm25"] > 0
        assert all(not x["id"].startswith("crowd_") for x in r["semantic"])
    finally:
        store._q("MATCH (n:Memory {user: $other}) DETACH DELETE n", other=other)


def test_keyword_agreement_moves_a_match_up(life):
    """Both rankings are shown in the trace: the fused order is what the prompt gets."""
    r = life.recall("is Rex still scared of thunderstorms?", today=T, touch=False)
    top = r["semantic"][0]
    assert top["text"] == "Pytest's dog Rex is afraid of thunderstorms"
    assert top["keyword_rank"] == 1 and top["fused"] == max(x["fused"] for x in r["semantic"])


def test_a_message_without_words_still_recalls(life):
    r = life.recall("?!", today=T, touch=False)
    assert all(x["keyword_rank"] is None for x in r["semantic"])
